Release 0.5.0 — the governance canon release. It moved specs_pattern_version 5 to 6 and made the bug-recurrence loop measurable instead of argued. Six backlog entries were consumed (specs-canon-v6, entity-behavior-map, bug-lineage-and-commit-discipline, audit-canon-v1, memory-two-tier-principles, dd-diagnose) across FR1-FR22 in four segments S1-S4, zero bugs picked (AS-4). What landed: (1) the v6 canon root plus TREE-8 as a WARN-only conformance check and `specs doctor --recipe` rendering ordered steps off the same finding objects `--json` emits; (2) `BUGS.jsonl` as one record per bug with a three-category field split, a closed `surface` enum single-sourced from the feature-package inventory, and ONE write seam over a generic id-keyed record store; (3) the whole historical ledger migrated with `registration_commit`/`resolved_commit` derived from an all-refs git walk, plus a permanent pure derivation in `core/bug_provenance.py`; (4) `RELEASE.jsonl` retiring `ACTIVE.md` and `CLOSURE.md`, with one fold and one reader; (5) `BACKLOG.md` as a live photo with exits in `backlog_histo.jsonl`; (6) `dd-diagnose` carrying the lineage duty as phase 0; (7) hooks de-slopped to the publication boundary — pre-commit always exits 0, pre-push refuses exactly three things; (8) `behavior-map.json` retiring `rules-skills-map.json` with 28 rows over 22 skills and 16 scoped AGENTS.md sources, RED in five directions; (9) audits as committed spec artifacts with three pillars over a sha window, and the first audit run on this repository as a dry run; (10) the memory trio split into ADR-gated Part 1 principles and a freely-editable Part 2, with 28 ADRs authored `proposed`. Deliberately NOT shipped: `specs upgrade` was not grown (its complexity is pinned, the case-only renames are recipe steps run by hand), no new blocking CLI validation or hook block was added anywhere (D15), and the FR16 audit opens no remediation release — its findings go to intake and the NEXT release binds them (AS-10).

DRIFT 1 — FR15's declared direction does not match its measurement (an A22.3 defect, operator disposition owed). FR15 declared itself net-negative at roughly -200 LOC together with T-050-25A. Measured: the two task commits together are net +42 (T-050-25 alone +108/-53 = +55; T-050-25A alone +159/-172 = -13, and dual-attributed FR15/FR4). Widening to every FR15-named file across the whole release range gives +645/-409 = net +236 — the same direction, larger. A positive net inside an FR that declared itself net-negative is a defect by A22.3's own words. The declaration is what was wrong, not the work: the sibling claims of that FR (regex-over-prose count down roughly 59 percent, four SPEC-DOC codes retired, `#doctor` complexity 30 to 10) all hold, and converting prose regexes into a structured JSONL fold added helper and dataclass code the estimate never anticipated. Recorded for the operator to disposition; nothing is retro-edited to make the number agree.

DRIFT 2 — A12.5's wording is true only under its narrowest reading. A12.5 states `AI-surface LOC net for S2 is negative`. Measured at three scopes: FR12 alone reads -1; the A22.4-named FR7+FR11+FR12 scope reads +203; the whole-S2 total reads +544. The acceptance is satisfied only by the first. This is a spec-wording call for `product-engineer` and the operator, not further engineering — the honest statement is that S2 grew the AI surface while moving procedure out of prose into pointers, and that both the file count and the line count are reported rather than only the falling one. Carried forward unresolved, per the S2 re-verdict and the release verdict that both named it.

DRIFT 3 — AS-16 was resolved toward option (i), the CLI verb. The SPEC left the record-store seam's EXPOSURE operator-gated between (i) one CLI verb and (ii) a skill-invoked Python entry point, and recommended (i). Option (i) was taken: `dadaia bugs update --set key=value` is the one governance-write door and `dadaia bugs archive` is its idempotent 90-day sweep, so the verb surface is `append | status | stats | update | archive`. The leaf arithmetic stays neutral because T-050-21A deleted `specs release open` and `specs segment open`, both dead once the phase became a fold. The seam itself is unchanged either way: three writers (registration, resolution, the audit's provenance rewrite) all go through `features/bugs`'s record store, so redaction, atomicity and refuse-stale hold on the executed path for every writer and not only for the CLI.

DRIFT 4 — AS-17's three public-assets single-source engines are deferred, out loud. The doctor byte goldens, `shipped-hashes.json`, and the two projection authorities were named as deferred at definition and are NOT built by this release; only FR10A's bounded deletion-only slice landed, and it measured N=0 because the roster class it targeted had already been retired by the previous release. The live cost during S1-S4 is measured rather than assumed: exactly 1 bug with `surface: public-assets` was registered in the window (`skill-docs-cite-retired-bugs-append-event-flag`, since resolved). The deferral carries a named intake target — `public-assets-single-source-engines` — because a deferral without a named target is what produced four of that surface's eighteen prior bugs.

DRIFT 5 — three operator-gated tasks are unstarted and block a clean ship, by design not by omission. T-050-02: the definition PR has not been opened because the branch is unpushed, so the `defined` milestone's `pr` field stays null and is filled when that PR merges. T-050-14: the tag-then-delete of the root `specs/_archive/` is destructive and runs only with the operator present — its open marker is the single TREE-8 warning `specs doctor` reports today, and the SCAFFOLD tests in `tests/integration/test_consumed_backlog_relocation.py` retire with it. T-050-31: the ADR acceptance sitting has not happened, so all 28 inventory ADRs remain `proposed` — no agent may flip a Status to `accepted`, and until the operator sits, every Part-1 principle in the memory trio reads `ADR: NNNN (proposed)`. None of the three is a defect; each is a gate the release cannot pass on its own authority.

DRIFT 6 — concurrent sessions shared one git index and contaminated commit boundaries. Two bugs are registered and still open: `concurrent-sessions-share-git-index-commit-boundary-contamination` and `concurrent-agent-git-add-clobbers-other-sessions-staged-files-into-unrelated-commit`. The observable cost inside this release: two measurement captures had to be RE-TAKEN after another session's in-flight work landed mid-run (an early `ci preflight` recorded three pytest failures traceable entirely to an uncommitted compare-then-swap WIP, superseded by a clean re-run), and the release QA verdict recorded a further +10 test functions / +1 file of drift accruing between the invariants capture and its own HEAD. This is the no-locks doctrine working as designed — races surface rather than being prevented — but the isolated-commit-shape discipline (FR8) depends on staging being scoped, and a shared index defeats that. Both bugs go to intake; neither is closed by this release.

DRIFT 7 — rc-1 is planned as the FINAL rc, and that plan is untested. `feature/0.5.0` was unpushed for the entire S1-S4 window: no CI ran, no `develop` merge happened, and therefore no rc round has burned. The whole implemented scope was validated locally and closed by QA, so rc-1 opens and closes at the operator's first push-and-merge, and the ladder collapses to one candidate. Two honest consequences follow. First, every CI-observable claim is unobserved by construction, including the standing `windows-xdist-workers-crash-on-unit-fast-tier` observation (LOW, open, unpicked per AS-4) — its non-recurrence this release means nothing, since zero CI runs occurred. Second, if exercising the merged `develop` finds a defect, rc-2 opens and this closure record is superseded by the one written at the real final rc. The archive move (T-050-41) therefore waits on the rc-1 merge, never precedes it.

The release QA verdict read all 29 added test files plus the one renamed file in full against the admission filter and found NO legitimate closure: every new function targets genuinely new or genuinely changed surface, and where two files test related ground the split is cross-referenced in their docstrings. Deletions that did happen were deletions WITH their subject, each under a named verdict: the pre-commit backlog-scoping integration test and its e2e companion (FR9 deleted the block they assert — the release's one LARGE-tier removal with no replacement at that tier, replaced instead by three cheaper contract fixtures), the whole `test_rules_skills_map.py` file (renamed-and-extended into `test_behavior_map.py`, proven by a name-diff with zero residue), the BugEvent-subject unit files, the BL-DUP cases (the invariant became structurally impossible), and the CLOSURE-parsing doctor cases with their golden entries curated rather than regenerated. Deleting any of them now would violate the expiry discipline itself; all three are KEEP-WITH-REASON, flagged for automatic re-review at 0.6.0's closure. One newly registered LOW flake (`test-v30-pyramid-shape-collect-only-subprocess-times-out-under-nauto-contention`, observed pass and fail on the same code under `-n auto` CPU contention) was registered rather than silently retried, and its quarantine-marking is handed to `software-engineer`, since qa-engineer rules and does not edit test files. V31's fix is named: the mutation baseline's isolated venv must either widen its install list to cover `core/models/`'s real transitive deps or its documented stdlib-only scope invariant must be corrected — two bugs name that gap from two angles.

The sweep is owed at RC-FLOW step 11, after the disposition sweep and before the archive move, and it is scoped to THIS release's own runtime artifacts under `.dadaia/` — never to anything committed. In scope: the release's own reports and handoffs under `.dadaia/reports/dadaia-workspace/**` and `.dadaia/handoff/dadaia-workspace/**`, and the `.dadaia/tmp/<agent>/20260827/` capture lanes (the T-050-03 baselines, the T-050-34 invariants capture and its per-check logs, the FR3 migration report and the FR4 back-fill report). Two rules bound it. First, a consumed COORDINATION handoff is deleted by its consumer; an ARTIFACT-BEARING handoff is exempt and follows its report's retention — the operator-facing intake report and its handoff survive this sweep. Second, nothing in `specs/` is touched: every number those temp captures produced that a later reader needs is restated in the notes of this record precisely because that lane is GC'd at three days and a path is never a citation. Log writers under `.dadaia/logs/` rotate at write time under their own writers and are not swept here.

MOVE. At T-050-41, after the rc-1 merge and after the disposition and artifact sweeps, `specs/releases/0.5.0/` moves by `git mv` to `specs/releases/_archive/0.5.0/` — the per-area archive this release created, never the root `specs/_archive/` that FR6 retires. The move is a `git mv` and not a file-tool write, and the whole SPEC/PLAN/TASKS/RELEASE.jsonl/reviews/verdicts set travels together; the CI verdict gate resolves evidence at that new path because its evidence roots and its release-id pattern are derived from the canon rather than from hard-coded globs. `phase: ARCHIVED` is appended as the last record of this stream. Two ordering rules hold: the six-axis code review already ran on the thawed tree BEFORE the move, and the move happens only once no finding of this release's own disposition sweep is left non-terminal. The next release starts fresh with its own `RELEASE.jsonl` — there is nothing to repoint.
